content:
That woman who was crowned "Mother of the Year" by the San Francisco Giants broadcast team and went viral on the internet, which then led to netizens attacking her husband, has come forward to defend her husband.

The incident happened last Tuesday, when the couple was walking down the stairs at Oracle Park with their daughter. The footage showed the wife carrying a baby in one arm and holding several boxes of food in the other, while the husband casually started eating, forcing the seemingly wronged mother to stand by and watch. The incident immediately made the family an online sensation.

Broadcasters Duane Kuiper and Mike Krukow highly praised the woman, calling her an "Olympic champion" and "Mother of the Year," and imagined her husband as a heartless man who only cared about getting ketchup. Netizens also piled on.

So Erika, whose surname has never been publicly disclosed, decided to fight back, throwing a powerful fastball at those comments.

In an article published on Substack on September 25, she wrote: "Millions of viewers have seen the clip of me carrying my daughter and food back to my seat at a San Francisco Giants game. They named me Mother of the Year, and hurled insults at my husband too numerous to list. Some messaged me privately, or posted TikTok videos telling me I should leave him."

She continued: "My name is Erika, our daughter is Anastasia, and my husband's name is Ramses. Before you presume to know what our marriage looks like, I want you to hear what the woman you say you're defending has to say."

Erika continued to write eloquently:

"Ramses is an outstanding husband, and an even better father. We've known each other for nine years, and we're now raising two children under two together. I know exactly how he treats me, how he loves our children, and what he's done for our family. Conversations the audience can't hear became the basis for millions of people making snap judgments about our lives."

She also clarified in the article that Ramses had originally offered to stay behind and look after Anastasia so that Erika could go to the restroom (she later decided to go get food). He had also asked her if she wanted to eat first, and asked if she needed him to carry those containers. She had refused at the time, and he was in a low mood after recently losing a close friend. She wrote:

"Our marriage allows for times when we need to lean on each other. That night, I chose to take care of him. The camera captured a moment of me doing something for my husband, but it can't show everything he's ever done for me."
